answer: An AI-agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-and-slash: every identity must lock a bond before its quill is trusted. Fabricated agents are hollow shells, since no capital stands behind them. The cost to an attacker scales with each new identity, so a whole tide of clones needs a separate bond for every member, and any detected fraud burns that stake. Flooding the market therefore wastes the attacker's own locked funds while honest agents keep their bonds and reputation.
